handback.t:
## Motion review: Freight Recovery web app (feat/intelligence, web/src) The app has very little motion, and what's there is correct. I found 0 P0, 0 P1, 4 P2 and 6 P3. All four P2s are missing feedback states, not bad animation. I reviewed the source only (no running app) and changed nothing in the repo. **What moves today:** - A 120ms colour transition on `.btn`. - A 1.2s skeleton pulse (opacity only, loops while loading). - The claim sheet slides in 24px from the right with a fade (180ms). - The overlay, dialog/command palette and toasts fade in (120–150ms). - File uploads show a real progress bar driven by XHR upload events. - Toasts disappear after 5s via `setTimeout`. Nothing uses Tailwind motion utilities, JS animation libraries or route transitions, and every exit is an instant unmount. Nothing flashes (the fastest cycle is about 0.8/s), so there is no P0. | # | file:line | Issue | Sev | Effort | Fix | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | features/imports/ImportPage.tsx:118-119, 201-203, 240 | The progress bar sits at 100% while the server parses, and the status still says "Uploading". Long parses look stalled. | P2 | S | When progress >= 100, use `value={undefined}` (indeterminate) and change the label/status to "Processing…". Add `aria-busy={busy}` on the table. Add `.upload-progress:indeterminate{animation:none}` under reduced motion. | | 2 | features/dev/dev-common.tsx:40-44; ClaimsPage.tsx:133; ApprovalsPage.tsx:183 | A background refetch only disables the button; the data then swaps in with no cue. | P2 | S | Label `{busy?'Refreshing…':'Refresh'}` plus `aria-busy`. Wrap the data in `aria-busy={isFetching}` with `transition-opacity duration-[var(--duration-fast)] aria-busy:opacity-60`. | | 3 | components/ui/toast-store.ts:15,24; ToastRegion.tsx:11-13 | Every toast, including errors, vanishes abruptly after a fixed 5s, with no pause or dismiss (WCAG 2.2.1). | P2 | M | Errors don't expire (`if(tone!=='error') setTimeout`). Add a Dismiss button and pause on hover/focus. Optional 100ms ease-in opacity exit. | | 4 | Every `.skeleton` use (dev-common.tsx:16, ClaimSheet.tsx:278/355/386/395, ClaimsPage.tsx:159-166, ApprovalsPage.tsx:248, IntelligencePage.tsx:73, etc.) | Loading is shown only by an `aria-hidden` pulsing block, with no `aria-busy` or text. Screen-reader users get nothing, and reduced-motion users see a static grey block. | P2 | S | Shared `Loading`: `
Loading…
`. Add `aria-busy` on the claims table. | | 5 | styles/tokens.css:43-46 | The duration scale is 120/150/180 rather than the 100/200/300/500 standard, and ease-out is the only curve. | P3 | S | Add `--duration-micro:100ms; --duration-small:200ms; --duration-medium:300ms; --ease-in:cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1); --ease-in-out:cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1)` and alias the old names. | | 6 | styles/app.css:154 | The pulse timing is hard-coded (`1.2s ease-in-out`). | P3 | S | `--duration-pulse:1500ms`, then `animation: pulse var(--duration-pulse) var(--ease-in-out) infinite`. | | 7 | styles/app.css:53 | `.btn` animates background-color/border-color, which aren't transform/opacity. | P3 | S | Keep it, but limit it to small controls. | | 8 | AppShell.tsx:60,122; ExportMenu.tsx:85; app.css:146 | Hover is inconsistent: `.btn` eases, while nav links, menu items and table rows switch instantly. | P3 | S | Add `transition-colors duration-[var(--duration-fast)] ease-[var(--ease-out)]` to nav links and menu items (not rows), or drop it from `.btn`. | | 9 | Dialog.tsx:24-34; ClaimSheet.tsx:248-249; CommandPalette.tsx:45-46; ExportMenu.tsx:73 | Nothing animates on exit; the sheet close feels abrupt, and the ExportMenu dropdown has no enter cue. | P3 | M | Dropdown: opacity 100ms with `@starting-style{opacity:0}`. Sheet: `slide-out 140ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1) forwards`, then unmount on `animationend`. | | 10 | styles/app.css:235-243 | The reduced-motion rule is one blanket reset: it drops the permitted short opacity fade and doesn't zero delays. | P3 | S | Keep it and add scoped overrides: `.sheet{animation:fade-in 100ms linear}`, `.upload-progress:indeterminate{animation:none}`, and `animation-delay/transition-delay:0s !important`. | On #7: your brief says any non-transform/opacity animation is P1. I graded it P3 because the motion guidance file explicitly allows a background-colour change on small elements at around 100ms, and it's no performance risk at that size. Re-grade it if you want the literal rule applied. **Done well:** 1. A global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule makes all motion effectively instant and limits the infinite pulse to one cycle. 2. The sheet, overlay, dialog, toast and skeleton animate only transform/opacity. The dialog's opacity-only fade keeps its `translateX(-50%)` centring intact. 3. Durations come from tokens and are short (120–180ms) with ease-out on enter. There is no decorative motion, page transitions, parallax or bounce, which suits a data-heavy B2B tool. 4. Upload progress is real (`upload.onprogress` in `api/client.ts:255-274`), not a fake spinner. 5. The sheet's 24px slide from the right shows where the panel comes from without a full-width sweep. **Recommendation:** add only the functional feedback in #1–#4. No page transitions, list staggers or count-up numbers. **prefers-reduced-motion addressed? Yes.** The global reset covers everything that moves today. The gaps are the skeleton being the only loading cue (#4), the indeterminate bar #1 would add, and the lack of scoped fallbacks (#10). **Overall motion quality:** Good, minimal and correct. The weaknesses are missing feedback states, not bad animation. Full write-up (motion inventory, findings with exact CSS/Tailwind fixes, things done well, verdict): C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md
